questions.prompt: A material has stress \(60\,\mathrm{MPa}\) and strain \(3.0\times10^{-4}\). Find Young's modulus.
State the modulus used for a change in volume under pressure.
questions.answer: A volume change under pressure is described by the bulk modulus \(B\).

questions.prompt: A wire has \(Y=1.6\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{Pa}\), \(L=2.0\,\mathrm{m}\), \(A=3.0\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{m^2}\), and load \(480\,\mathrm{N}\). Find its extension.
A block has shear modulus \(G=8.0\times10^{9}\,\mathrm{Pa}\) and shear strain \(2.0\times10^{-5}\). Find the shear stress.
Pressure on a liquid increases by \(4.5\,\mathrm{MPa}\). Its bulk modulus is \(1.5\,\mathrm{GPa}\). Find \(\Delta V/V\).
A rod has \(Y=70\,\mathrm{GPa}\), area \(5.0\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{m^2}\), and length \(0.80\,\mathrm{m}\). Find its axial stiffness \(k_{\mathrm{axial}}\).
Two wires have the same material and length. Wire A has twice the area of wire B. Compare their axial stiffnesses and extensions under the same load.
questions.answer:
Axial stiffness is \(k=YA/L\). With the same \(Y\) and \(L\),
\[
k_A=2k_B
\]
For the same load \(F\), extension is \(\Delta L=F/k\), so
\[
\Delta L_A=\frac{1}{2}\Delta L_B
\]

questions.prompt: A \(1.0\,\mathrm{m}\) steel wire with \(Y=2.0\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{Pa}\) must extend by no more than \(1.0\,\mathrm{mm}\) under \(500\,\mathrm{N}\). Find the minimum area.

Two rods of equal length \(L\) are fixed between the same rigid plates and carry a total tensile load \(P\). Rod 1 has \(Y_1,A_1\); rod 2 has \(Y_2,A_2\). Derive each rod's load share and the common extension. State assumptions and interpret the stiffer-rod limit.
questions.answer:
Assume the plates are rigid, both rods remain elastic, and both rods have the same extension \(\Delta L\). Their stiffnesses are
\[
k_1=\frac{Y_1A_1}{L},\qquad k_2=\frac{Y_2A_2}{L}
\]
The total load is
\[
P=(k_1+k_2)\Delta L
\]
\[
\Delta L=\frac{P}{k_1+k_2}
\]
The load shares are
\[
F_1=k_1\Delta L=\frac{k_1}{k_1+k_2}P
\]
\[
F_2=\frac{k_2}{k_1+k_2}P
\]
If one rod is much stiffer, it carries nearly all the load while the common extension stays small.

questions.prompt: Two axial members are connected in series and carry the same tensile load \(P\). Member \(i\) has \(Y_i,A_i,L_i\). Derive the equivalent axial stiffness and a symbolic condition for total extension to stay below \(\delta_{\max}\). State assumptions and interpret which member dominates compliance.
questions.answer:
Assume linear elasticity, axial loading, and perfect series connection, so both members carry load \(P\). Each extension is
\[
\Delta L_i=\frac{PL_i}{Y_iA_i}
\]
Total extension is
\[
\delta=P\left(\frac{L_1}{Y_1A_1}+\frac{L_2}{Y_2A_2}\right)
\]
Thus the equivalent stiffness is
\[
k_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{P}{\delta}=\left(\frac{L_1}{Y_1A_1}+\frac{L_2}{Y_2A_2}\right)^{-1}
\]
The extension condition is
\[
P\left(\frac{L_1}{Y_1A_1}+\frac{L_2}{Y_2A_2}\right)\le\delta_{\max}
\]
The member with the larger compliance term \(L_i/(Y_iA_i)\) dominates the total stretch.
